newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokai Kogyo applies for court protection - Teikoku.
newsitem.headline: Tokai Kogyo applies for court protection - Teikoku.

text.p: Japanese construction company Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd applied for court protection under Japanese bankruptcy laws at Tokyo District Court on Friday afternoon, private credit research firm Teikoku Databank Ltd said.
Tokai's debts totalled 510 billion yen, Teikoku said.
Both Tokai Kogyo and the court declined to comment whether or not Tokai Kogyo had filed the application.

Teikoku said in a statement that Tokai made the application after failing to win necessary financial support from its four major banks -- Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd, Tokai Bank Ltd, Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, Norinchukin Bank.

Teikoku said Tokai's business deteriorated after the bursting of Japan's late-1980's "bubble" of inflated asset prices, which led to problems with the company's real estate development projects as well as to bankruptcies of firms to which Tokai had guaranteed loans.

Teikoku said that in November 1993, Tokai drafted a comprehensive plan to rebuild its business by trimming interest-bearing debt and reduce its workforce, while urging its main creditor banks to lower interest rates on loans.
The prolonged slump in Japan's property market, however, made it difficult for the company to recover, it added.
Teikoku said Tokai's business failure was the eighth biggest in terms of debt in Japan's post-war history, and the first ever failure of a listed general contractor.
